Browser support

Device Chrome / Edge Safari / Firefox
Windows ✓ Yes ✗ No
macOS ✓ Yes ✗ No
Android ✓ Yes ✗ No
Linux ✓ Yes ✗ No
iOS ✗ No ✗ No
iPadOS ✗ No ✗ No
Why iOS and iPadOS can't support this: Apple requires all browsers on iOS and iPadOS to use Safari's engine. Even Chrome or Edge on these devices run on top of Safari underneath — and Safari doesn't support the File System Access API.
Alternatives that work everywhere: Use Google Drive or Network location / NAS — both use standard web requests and work on every browser and device.

How the projection works

The dashed line estimates the next three months from your recent saving pattern. On a short range it may show fewer, so the estimate never crowds out the history it came from.

  • It uses your net saved per month over the last 12 completed months (the current, part-way month is ignored).
  • One-off months are trimmed, so a single unusually large deposit or withdrawal won’t skew the forecast.
  • A trend line is fitted with more weight on recent months, so it follows your latest momentum.
  • The slope is dampened to avoid over-confident predictions.
  • The shaded band is the uncertainty range, widening the further ahead it looks.

It’s an estimate, not a guarantee — real results will vary.

AI import — privacy

⚠ Before using AI import, please be aware:

When you import a file, its contents — including transaction amounts, dates, and merchant names — are sent to the AI provider you've selected. This data leaves your device and is processed on that provider's servers.

Your API key is saved in your backup (Google Drive, network location or file). Without encryption, anyone who can open that backup could read your key.

Vault does not store or transmit your files or API keys to its own servers. Your original files are never modified or deleted.

Provider privacy policies:

Each provider has its own data handling practices. Please review their privacy policy before use, as policies may change over time.

Privacy policy

Legal
Your data stays yours.
Vault is built on a simple principle: your financial data belongs to you. We do not collect it, store it, or have any access to it.
Effective date: 1 January 2025  ·  Last updated: November 2026
No data collection
No personal data is transmitted to any server we operate.
Stays on your device
Your data is stored in your browser and in the backup location you choose. It only goes elsewhere when you use AI import.
No ads or tracking
No analytics, no advertising, and no third-party tracking of any kind.
Your backup, your choice
Google Drive backup is entirely optional. Your file, your account, your control.
01
Who we are

Vault is a personal savings tracker available at vaultsavings.app. It is an independent application with no corporate entity behind it.

02
What data Vault collects

Vault collects no personal data. The app has no database and no analytics. Your transactions never reach us.

Everything you enter — transactions, amounts, dates and settings — is stored in your browser on your own device. It only leaves your device when you connect a backup, or when you use AI import (see section 06).

In plain terms: We cannot see your data. We do not have it and we never receive it. If you cleared your browser storage right now, your Vault data would be permanently gone — there is no copy we could restore.
03
Google Drive backup

Vault offers an optional Google Drive backup. Connecting Google Drive is not required to use Vault. If you do choose to connect it, the following applies:

Scope of access: Vault requests only the drive.file permission — the most restricted scope available. This grants Vault access solely to files that Vault itself created. Vault cannot read, modify, or access any other file in your Google Drive.

What is stored: A single file named vault-data.json containing your transaction data. If you have enabled encryption, this file is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to Drive, so the contents are protected even within your own Drive.

What Vault does not access: Vault does not request access to your Google profile, email address, contacts, calendar, or any other Google service.

Sign-in relay: Google requires a secret to complete sign-in that can't be kept safely inside a web page. So the sign-in codes Google issues pass through a small relay Vault runs on Cloudflare Workers, which swaps them for access tokens with Google. Your transactions and backup file never pass through it.

Your Drive file is yours. You can view, download, or delete it at any time directly from Google Drive. Disconnecting Drive within Vault stops future syncing but does not delete the file.
04
Local file and network backup

Vault also supports saving to a local file on your device or to a network location such as a NAS or WebDAV server. These backups are written directly from your browser to your chosen destination. No data passes through any server we operate.

05
Cookies and tracking

Vault uses no cookies, no analytics platforms, no advertising networks, and no third-party tracking scripts of any kind. It uses three standard browser storage features, all kept on your device: localStorage for your data and settings, IndexedDB to remember a linked backup file, and sessionStorage briefly during Google sign-in.

06
Data sharing and third parties

We do not share data with third parties because we do not hold any of your data. Vault talks to these outside services:

Exchange rates — ExchangeRate-API (open.er-api.com) and frankfurter.dev, for daily currency rates. These requests contain only currency codes, never your amounts.

Google APIs — only when you connect Google Drive backup, through the sign-in relay described in section 03. Governed by Google's own Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Your AI provider — only when you use AI import. The file you import (its transactions, amounts, dates and merchant names) is sent to the provider you chose, under that provider's privacy policy.

cdnjs (Cloudflare) — only during import, to load the PDF reader and, for older spreadsheet formats, the full spreadsheet reader. No data of yours is sent.

Fonts and the spreadsheet library used for exports are built into Vault, so nothing else is fetched.

07
Encryption

Vault offers optional AES-256-GCM encryption for backup files. When enabled, your data is encrypted entirely within the browser before being written to any backup destination. The encryption key is derived from your chosen password and never leaves your device.

When you set a password, a recovery key file is downloaded automatically. This is the only way to recover your data if you forget your password — Vault holds no record of your password or encryption key and cannot recover your data on your behalf.

08
Children's privacy

Vault is a general-purpose financial tracking tool and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect information from anyone under the age of 13.

09
Changes to this policy

If this policy changes in a material way, the effective date at the top of this page will be updated. As Vault has no account system, we are unable to notify users directly — we encourage you to review this page occasionally.

Questions?
If you have any questions about this privacy policy or how Vault handles data, please contact us at privacy@vaultsavings.app.

01
What is Vault?

Vault is an independent, single-file web application for tracking personal savings. It runs in your browser with no account and no subscription. It is available at vaultsavings.app.

Vault is built for people who want a clear picture of their savings without handing their data over to anyone else. Everything you enter stays on your device unless you explicitly connect a backup of your choosing.

02
Independent, and works offline

Vault is an independent project with no corporate entity behind it. It is not affiliated with any financial institution, investment platform, or data company.

The app is a single HTML file with no build step and no framework, and you can read every line of it. Its fonts and spreadsheet export are built in, so it works offline. Only exchange rates, backup sync and AI import need a connection; without one, Vault uses the last rates it saved.

03
Currency data

Vault converts between currencies with daily rates from ExchangeRate-API. The FX Impact card and Currency Exposure's year-ago comparison use daily reference rates from frankfurter.dev, so both ends of a comparison come from the same source. Rates are saved in your backup, so other devices and later sessions reuse them instead of fetching them again.

Attribution: Exchange rate data is provided by ExchangeRate-API and Frankfurter. Rates are indicative, updated daily, and for information only.
04
Acknowledgements

Fonts: Vault uses DM Serif Display and DM Sans, built into the app. Both are open source typefaces designed by Colophon Foundry and released under the SIL Open Font Licence.

Spreadsheets: SheetJS Community Edition, released under the Apache 2.0 licence.

Exchange rates: Daily currency exchange rate data is provided by ExchangeRate-API and Frankfurter.

Icons: All icons in Vault are custom SVG elements designed specifically for the app.

05
Disclaimer

Vault is a personal tracking tool only. It does not provide financial advice, investment recommendations, or tax guidance. Exchange rates displayed in the app are indicative only and should not be used for commercial currency conversion.
